title: Birbal and the Barbers (Português)
summary: The barbers of Agra spread wild rumors that send commodity prices soaring. Birbal teaches the guild a humorous lesson in accountability. [PT]
full_text:
The barbers of Agra were the social heart of the city; while shaving beards and massaging heads, they shared news, political rumors, and market gossip. However, several unscrupulous barbers began inventing wild rumors—claiming that the salt supply was exhausted, or that the Emperor was banning grain trade—causing panicked citizens to hoard food, doubling prices in the bazaar.

Akbar asked Birbal to curb the dangerous rumor-mongering without restricting free speech.

Birbal summoned the leaders of the barbers' guild to the palace. With a very grave face, Birbal announced:

'Brothers, I have an urgent imperial assignment for your guild. His Majesty has decreed that next week, the imperial treasury will reward every barber in Agra with one gold coin for every genuine piece of news he brings to court.

'However, to ensure accuracy, if any rumor brought by a barber turns out to be false, the barber must forfeit one ear to the royal executioner!'

The barbers looked at each other in sheer terror!

'One ear?' the guildmaster stammered. 'My lord, gossip is only talk! We only repeat what we hear in the morning breeze!'

'Then let your morning breeze be silent, or verify your facts before you speak!' Birbal smiled sharply. 'If you are unwilling to risk your own ear for your words, do not risk the livelihoods of fifty thousand citizens with reckless rumors!'

The barbers bowed low, apologized, and returned to their shops. From that day, the barbers of Agra spoke only of the weather and hair oil, and market prices returned to stability. Akbar commended Birbal for solving the civic crisis with humor and firmness.
